content_of_post_to_answer: How did basic training contribute to your mental transition from childhood to adulthood?
answer: Basic training often changes people less through hardship itself and more through the shift in responsibility it creates. Childhood is largely shaped by having others manage consequences for you; adulthood begins when your choices, habits, and reactions become your own responsibility. The overlooked part is that discipline learned in training is not just about following orders—it is about discovering that you can function under pressure without depending on comfort or constant reassurance. The real transition is not becoming tougher; it is learning to trust yourself when nobody is there to carry you.
